classification.difficultyReason: Uses replacement to identify independent draws, distinguishes either order from a specified order, and combines the two mutually exclusive parity orders.

content.prompt: Discs with the digits 0 to 9 are placed in a box. A disc is drawn at random, its digit is recorded, then it is replaced in the box. A second disc is then drawn and its digit is recorded. Find the probability:

children.label: a
children.prompt: that the two digits are the same

answer.worked:
Replacement gives $10\times10=100$ equally likely ordered pairs. The matching pairs are $(0,0),(1,1),\ldots,(9,9)$, so there are 10 favourable outcomes.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{same digits})&=\frac{10}{100}\\P(\text{same digits})&=\frac{1}{10}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: of drawing an even digit and an odd digit

answer.worked:
There are five even digits, including 0, and five odd digits. Replacement makes the draws independent. Either order is possible, and the two orders are mutually exclusive.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{one even and one odd})&=\frac{5}{10}\times\frac{5}{10}+\frac{5}{10}\times\frac{5}{10}\\P(\text{one even and one odd})&=\frac{50}{100}\\P(\text{one even and one odd})&=\frac{1}{2}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: that the first digit is a 6 and the second digit is odd

answer.worked:
The probability of drawing 6 first is $\frac{1}{10}$. After replacement, five of the ten digits are odd.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{6 first and odd second})&=\frac{1}{10}\times\frac{5}{10}\\P(\text{6 first and odd second})&=\frac{1}{20}\end{align*}$$
